title: This House by James Graham - review
transcript: this house by James Graham which I saw at church just a festival theater is set in the 1970s when Labour was running minority governments but it's not about Wilson Callaghan or Thatcher it looks at the ordinary politicians and shows them as human beings I would never thought that day-to-day politics could be quite so tense the play is set in the whips offices and these are the people who organized the party members voting and they're living in traumatic times as labor struggles to maintain its majority and government many people some of the brexit voters and Trump supporters perhaps seem to be rebelling against the perceived coziness of the establishment the James groans play shows that there is a purpose to this comity to go behind the scenes and see that our democracy can only work by cooperation compromise is an eye opener but more than the drama and the lesson in democracy this house reveals MPs as real people with feelings the characters are funny sad triumphant and tragic they care passionately and still respect their opponents and act honorably I give it four stars you
